text:
sophia: Kicking off a priming/throughput probe for crucible-7b — quick sync? FP16 looks clean but I see int8 tail spikes at long ctxs.

bench-bot: auto-bench summary: model=crucible-7b, hw=A100-80GB, profiles tested=fp16,int8-fast; batch=[1,2,4,8], ctx=[512,1024,2048]. FP16: best throughput 320 tok/s (batch=4), p50 15ms, p99 55ms. int8-fast: throughput 420 tok/s (batch=8) but p99 210ms at ctx=2048. Full JSON: https://redwood.internal/bench/312/json

rahul: saw same on a dedicated node. Reproduced with quant profile "int8-fast". Tail appears after ~1s sustained streaming — smells like KV cache eviction or GC spikes.

alex: can you paste the exact bench command you ran? I want to verify batching window + warmup settings.

sophia: running this now — command I used:
```
rbench run --model crucible-7b --runtime rserve --profile int8-fast --batch-sizes 1,2,4,8 \
  --ctx-lens 512,1024,2048 --warmup 200 --measure p50,p95,p99 --out results/5421.json
```
Linking results after upload.

bench-bot: queued job 5421 (crucible-7b priming probe). ETA ~12m. Collectors: per-token latencies, kernel stall samples, memory highwater.

lisa: quick prioritization suggestion:
1) single-node single-stream ctx sweep (512/1024/2048) to isolate tail
2) throughput sweep batch=1..16 at ctx=512 for unit costs
3) warmup/priming test (cold vs warmed KV cache)
4) quant quality eval on evalset "prod-prompts-v2" for int8-fast and awq
If int8 quality drops >2% (ROUGE or exact-match proxy), hold rollout.

rahul: +1. Also add a warmup priming script: feed a 512-token prefix to populate caches, then measure steady-state latencies. I'll script it and push to tools/bench-scripts.

alex: edge-case to try: disable continuous batching to see if batch window growth causes the tail. add flag `--batch-window-ms 0` to test. Also try `--kv-prefetch true` to avoid on-demand evictions.

sophia: I'll take items 1 & 2 today, queue the quality eval tomorrow. Dropping a short checklist here: 
- [ ] ctx sweep (single-node, single-stream)
- [ ] throughput sweep (batch sizes)
- [ ] warmup priming test (cold vs warm)
- [ ] quant quality eval (int8-fast vs awq)
- [ ] upload plots + update runbook/dashboard link

bench-bot: job 5421 finished. Key takeaways: int8 p99 improved from 210ms -> 95ms after enabling `--kv-prefetch true` and bumping warmup to 400. FP16 unchanged. Artifacts: https://redwood.internal/bench/5421/json and dashboard https://redwood.internal/dashboard/bench/5421

rahul: nice improvement. can you attach p95/p99 plots? also please rerun with `--quant backend=awq` to compare AWQ vs int8-fast latency + quality.

sophia: attached plots to the doc, starting AWQ compare now. will report back with quality numbers (prod-prompts-v2) when done. thanks all :white_check_mark:
